meta.title: Echoes of Regret
meta.source: Piggy_AU_FULL_STORY_COMPLETE.txt (through THE END OF BOOK THREE) plus the fullest chapters 37-45

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: Welcome to *Echoes of Regret*. Your choices will shape the memories that remain. The infection does not erase who people were—it chains them to what they wish they could change.

Background: Dimly lit laboratory in the Lucella General Hospital annex. Glass vials line the shelves, some glowing with an unnatural green, others already turning a sickly red. Rain taps against the high windows. Mr. P, a tired man in a stained lab coat, stands before a bubbling apparatus. His hands shake as he adjusts a dial.

In the city of Lucella, Evalia, a man named Mr. P sought only to save his wife. The disease that ravaged her body left little time. The potion he created... was meant to heal. It was never meant to remember.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (whispering, almost to the empty air beside him) Just one more adjustment. For her. Only for her. If it works, she can come home. If it works, I can stop saying "I'm sorry" to an empty bed.
He pours a measured amount of the substance into a final vial. It bubbles violently, then settles into a deep, unnatural red. The liquid seems to pulse, as if it has a heartbeat.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mrs. P (distant memory, voiceover)
steps.text: Don't stay so late again, love. The house is too quiet without you.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (closing his eyes) I know. I'm sorry. I'm always sorry.

But perfection is a lie. What was meant to cure the body became the seed of an outbreak that would consume everything—bodies, minds, and the very regrets that define us. The potion did not erase pain. It amplified it. It forced the infected to live inside their worst "what if" until nothing else remained.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: The outbreak begins not with a scream, but with a whisper of regret. Your story starts three days later.

Scene: Rainy night outside the Piggy Residence. Streetlights flicker. The Player, a young police officer, steps out of a patrol car. Flashlight in hand, rain dripping from the brim of their hat. The house is dark except for a single light upstairs.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (internal monologue) Georgie Piggy. Eight years old. Missing for three days. Parents say he wandered off after an argument. But the call came from a neighbor who heard screaming. The house feels... wrong. Too quiet.
You approach the door. It creaks open before you touch it, as if the house itself is inviting you in—or warning you away.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Sound
steps.text: A low, wet snort from deep inside. Then the faint sound of a child's music box playing "Twinkle Twinkle."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Hello? Police. I'm here about Georgie. If anyone's inside, respond.

You step inside. The living room is chaotic—furniture overturned, family photos smashed on the floor, glass glittering in the flashlight beam. A baseball bat lies near the stairs, smeared with something dark. Upstairs, a light flickers.

options.label: Investigate the kitchen for signs of struggle
Head upstairs immediately toward the light
Call for backup before entering further
Search the living room for Georgie's belongings

steps.text: Main path: Investigate carefully, then head upstairs.
You move toward the stairs. Halfway up, something lunges from the shadows.
Penny Piggy, infected, swings a baseball bat with terrifying strength. Her eyes glow crimson. Her mouth is open in a snarl, but beneath it, her voice cracks with something else.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny (infected, distorted)
steps.text: Georgie... I shouldn't have yelled... I should have held his hand...

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (dodging) Penny! Stop! I'm police—I'm here to help!
The bat grazes your shoulder. You tumble down the last few steps. Darkness rushes in.
[Fade to black]
You awaken in a bedroom. The door is locked from outside. A note is pinned to the wall with a child's safety pin.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Note
steps.text: "They're not gone. They're just... remembering differently. Don't let them make you remember too."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (groaning, sitting up) What... happened? My head...
Outside the door, heavy footsteps. Then silence. Then a whisper.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny (through the door, almost clear)
steps.text: Georgie... where are you? I'm sorry I got angry. Please come out.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (quietly) She's still in there. Somewhere.

You find a key under the bed, next to a half-finished drawing of a family. You unlock the door carefully. Escaping the house takes every ounce of focus. The infected Penny patrols the hallway, but fragments of her voice echo—not only snarls, but whispers of a sister's name and a promise she broke.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (escaping through a side window, rain soaking through) I have to get to the station. Warn them. This isn't just a missing child. This is something else. Something that remembers.
As you run into the night, the house behind you is silent again—except for the music box, still playing for a brother who is no longer there.
End of Chapter 1
Scene: Lucella Police Station. Fluorescent lights buzz. Officer Doggy stands behind the desk, radio crackling with static. Rain drips from the Player's coat onto the floor.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: Player! You made it. Where's the kid? Dispatch said the house was a mess.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The house is compromised. Georgie's family... they're infected. Something's turning people. I saw Penny. She wasn't... herself. But she kept saying his name. She was sorry.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: (ears twitching, radio static growing louder) Infected? Like the reports from the outskirts? Mr. P's been handing out "medicine" door to door. Said it would help the sick. Free of charge. Too good to be true, but people were desperate.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Medicine that turns people into monsters who can still talk about what they regret?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: We need supplies. Gas for the car. Then we head out, find answers. And find Georgie if he's still alive. I've got a bad feeling about this.
You search the station. Infected begin to appear outside—neighbors, former officers, a delivery driver still holding a clipboard. Doggy grabs his baton, eyes hard.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: Stick close. We clear the armory, then the garage. If any of them are still talking, don't listen too long. It gets in your head.

options.label: Prioritize finding fuel and leave immediately
Search for any survivors or uninfected officers first
Barricade the doors and wait for more information
Check the radio logs for Mr. P's distribution routes

steps.text: Main path: Speed, but with caution.
In the garage, Doggy sips from a canteen left with the supply drop. His eyes flash red for a moment. He freezes.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: (coughing, gripping the counter) Tastes... off. The supply drop from Mr. P... he said it was just electrolyte water for the officers on long shifts.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Doggy? Don't drink that! Spit it out!

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: Too late. We move. Now. Before I can't.
You escape in the patrol car as the station falls. Infected officers smash against the garage door as you reverse out. Doggy drives, but his grip is unsteady. Rain streaks the windshield.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: If I turn... don't hesitate. Promise me. I've got a partner waiting at home. I told her I'd be back by midnight. I always tell her that.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: You're not turning. Not if I can help it. We'll find a way to stop this.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: (voice already strained) Just... keep driving. And if you see my badge later... give it to her. Tell her I tried.
End of Chapter 2
Scene: Abandoned art gallery on the edge of the city. Paintings of peaceful family life hang crooked, some slashed. The patrol car sputters and dies in the parking lot. Dawn is still hours away.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: Out of gas. We'll have to go on foot. The gallery was supposed to be a temporary shelter for the early cases. Looks like it didn't hold.

Inside, infected artists and visitors roam the halls. Some stand still, staring at their own paintings as if trying to remember why they made them. A cipher on a whiteboard reads: "We remember who we were. It hurts more."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (reading) They keep their memories? The infection doesn't wipe them clean?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: (voice strained, one hand pressed to his temple) Makes it worse. I can still hear my partner's voice. She's asking when I'm coming home. I should have called her.

You solve puzzles to open exits—aligning paintings that form a family portrait when correct, finding keys hidden in frames. Each correct alignment causes an infected nearby to pause, as if the completed image eases something.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: Player... my head. It's splitting. The regret... I left someone behind once. Years ago. A kid in a flood. I told myself I couldn't reach him. Is this punishment? Is that what this is?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Stay with me. We're getting out. You're not alone in this.
You reach the forest edge as Doggy collapses briefly, then rises with glowing eyes—but still speaking, still fighting.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: Go. Find the truth. Find the kid. I'll... hold them. Just this once, I won't leave anyone behind.
For a moment, he fights the infection through sheer will and the weight of every promise he ever made. Then he turns, buying you time as the infected close in.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (running into the trees) I'll come back for you. I swear. I'll come back.
End of Chapter 3
Scene: Dense forest at dawn. Mist clings to the trees. The Player stumbles through undergrowth, flashlight beam cutting through fog. Distant growls echo, but some of them sound like words.
The forest remembers every footstep that never returned. Every promise broken under these boughs. Every child who was told "stay close" and didn't.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (breathing hard) Doggy... I left him. He asked me not to hesitate. But I ran. Just like everyone else runs from their regrets.
You find a clearing. A small campsite—abandoned backpacks, a half-eaten sandwich, a child's shoe. A radio crackles.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Radio
steps.text: —anyone still out there? The infection's spreading from the city. If you hear this, head to the old school. Survivors are regrouping. Avoid the main roads. Avoid anyone who starts apologizing for things that already happened. Over—
Static cuts it off.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: School. Georgie might have gone that way. Kids love the woods... or fear them. Either way, he would have looked for somewhere familiar.

Infected deer-like figures (Bunny variants) patrol between trees. Their eyes glow, but one pauses, staring at a photo dropped on the ground—a picture of a family picnic. It reaches down, almost gently.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Bunny (whisper)
steps.text: Why did I leave...? I was only gone for a minute...
Even the animals carry fragments. Regret doesn't discriminate.

options.label: Approach the whispering infected carefully
Sneak past toward the radio tower for better signal
Search the campsite for supplies and the map first
Call out to see if any uninfected are nearby

steps.text: Main path: Search campsite, then sneak.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (whispering) If they remember, maybe some can be saved. But not now. Not alone.

You grab a map from the backpack. It marks the Lucella School, with a note in a child's handwriting: "Georgie was here. Scared of the dark. Left a teddy. Going to the school because Penny said the lights stay on."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: He's alive. Or was. I have to keep going.
As you move, an infected lunges. You fight it off with a branch, but its last words haunt you as it falls.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected
steps.text: I should have stayed... with her... I should have stayed...
Every infection is a story unfinished. Every regret a door that won't close.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (running toward the school path) I'm coming, Georgie. And I'm coming back for you too, Doggy. I won't make the same mistake twice.
End of Chapter 4

Scene: Lucella Elementary School. Hallways lined with faded drawings of families. Lockers hang open. The sound of a child's music box plays from somewhere deep inside the building. Morning light filters through broken windows.
Schools hold the purest regrets—the friends we outgrew, the words we never said, the futures we abandoned before they began. The infection loves this place.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Georgie... if you're here, I'm a friend. Not one of them. I'm here to take you somewhere safe.
You enter the cafeteria. Tables overturned. An infected teacher paces, holding a report card covered in red marks.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Teacher
steps.text: (muttering) Should have listened... should have protected them... I told them it was just a cold...
On a bulletin board: Missing posters. Georgie's is circled in red crayon. Next to it, a child's drawing of a smiling pig family. Underneath, a note.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (reading) "If anyone finds Georgie, tell him Mommy and Daddy are sorry. We didn't mean to scare him. We just wanted him to be careful."
The parents' regret reached him before the infection did.
You hear a small voice from a classroom at the end of the hall.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie (distant)
steps.text: Penny? Is that you? I don't want to play this game anymore... I'm sorry I ran. Please come back.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Georgie! It's the police. I'm here to help! You're not in trouble!
You rush in. Georgie is hiding under a desk, clutching a teddy bear. His eyes are normal—for now. But his arm has a faint red rash, and he flinches at every sound.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (scared) The monsters... they look like my family. But they say mean things. About how they regret having me. About how I made everything harder.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (kneeling) That's the infection talking. They love you. We're going to fix this. Together.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Mr. P said the medicine would make everyone better. He gave some to Penny. Then she... changed. She started saying sorry all the time. Even when nothing was wrong.

options.label: Reassure Georgie and escape immediately
Search the principal's office for more info on Mr. P
Ask Georgie what else he remembers about the day he left
Check the nurse's office for any uninfected staff or medical supplies

steps.text: Main path: Reassure, gather info, and move.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Stay close. We're getting out of here. Tell me everything you remember while we walk.
As you exit, an infected student blocks the way, whispering about a forgotten birthday party.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Student
steps.text: You never came... I waited...

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (clinging to you) Make them stop remembering the bad things. Please.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: I will. Or I'll stop the one who started this. Mr. P is going to answer for what he did.
In the school, innocence meets its first real regret—and chooses to keep moving anyway.
End of Chapter 5

Scene: Lucella General Hospital. The place where it began. Lights flicker over empty beds. IV bags hang like vines. A familiar lab coat is draped over a chair in the lobby. Georgie holds the Player's hand tightly.
Hospitals are temples of regret. Every "if only" is written in the charts. Every unfinished goodbye lives in the waiting rooms.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (with Georgie) This is where Mr. P worked. Where he tried to save his wife. Where he decided the rest of the city could live with the cost.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (quiet) Penny said Mrs. P was nice. She gave me candy once. She said sorry a lot too. Even before she got sick.
You find Mr. P's office. Notes everywhere. One journal entry stands out, written in increasingly shaky handwriting:

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Journal
steps.text: "The potion works on the body. But the mind... the mind remembers what it lost. My wife... she whispered my name even as her eyes changed. She kept saying she was sorry she got sick. Sorry she made me work so hard. I couldn't bear it. I kept going. I had to. If I can perfect the formula, maybe I can make the memories kind again. Maybe I can give her back the years we lost."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: He knew. He knew it kept their memories—and their regrets—and he kept distributing it. He thought he could fix the side effect later.
An infected nurse approaches, holding a baby rattle. She stops when she sees Georgie.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Nurse
steps.text: I should have been there... for my daughter... I told her I'd come after my shift...

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (hiding behind you) They all sound so sad.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The infection doesn't erase who they were. It amplifies what they wish they could change. It turns every "I should have" into a chain.
You find a sample of the original potion—red, glowing faintly. And a recording left on the desk.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mrs. P (recording)
steps.text: My love... if this works, we can be together. If it doesn't... don't blame yourself. Live. For both of us. Don't spend the rest of your life saying sorry to a ghost.
The greatest regret in the city belongs to the man who started it all. And he is still trying to outrun it.

options.label: Take the potion sample for study
Destroy the remaining samples
Look for a way to reverse the memory effect in the research notes
Play the recording for Georgie so he understands

steps.text: Main path: Take the sample and the recording. Vow to find a cure that addresses the regret, not just the body.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: We're not just fighting monsters. We're fighting the weight of every unfinished goodbye.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Can we make them forget the sad parts? Or... remember the good ones more?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (smiling faintly) That's the plan, kid. Now let's move. The city is calling. And Mr. P is somewhere in it.
End of Chapter 6
Scene: Underground metro station. Trains sit silent on the tracks. Flickering signs advertise "Escape the City—Start Fresh!" Posters are torn. The air is cold and still.
The metro was meant to carry people toward new beginnings. Now it only echoes the ones they left behind. Every delayed train is a life that never arrived.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (holding Georgie's hand) Stay between the lights. If we get separated, go to the surface exit and wait. Don't go looking for me.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Okay. I won't run this time. I promise.
Infected commuters wander the platforms, some still holding briefcases, muttering about missed meetings, forgotten anniversaries, children they didn't pick up from school.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Commuter
steps.text: I said I'd be home by six... I said I'd call...

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Every one of them had somewhere else to be. And now they're stuck here, saying sorry to no one.
You find a control room. A map shows the infection spreading fastest along the train lines—Mr. P used the metro to distribute "medicine" to the outer districts. Delivery schedules are marked in red.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: He didn't just create it. He delivered it. Door to door. Station to station. He made sure no one was left out.
A train suddenly activates, doors opening. Inside, an infected conductor grips the controls.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: All aboard... to the life you should have lived... the one you were supposed to have...

options.label: Board the train to reach the city center faster
Disable the train and walk the tracks
Use the PA system to try reasoning with the infected
Search the conductor's cabin for more distribution records

steps.text: Main path: Disable and proceed carefully, gathering more of Georgie's trust.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Player... do you have regrets?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (after a pause) Yeah. Leaving Doggy. Not getting to your house sooner. Promising people I'd come back when I don't know if I can. And now... promising you I'll get you home when I'm not sure what home looks like anymore.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Then don't make new ones. Stay with me. And when we find Penny, don't let her say sorry anymore. Just let her be my sister.
In the dark tunnels, a small voice becomes the anchor against the tide of collective regret.
End of Chapter 7

Scene: Abandoned carnival grounds. Lights still spin on the Ferris wheel, casting rainbows over empty stalls. The smell of stale popcorn mixes with something metallic. Georgie stops walking when he sees the prize booths.
Carnivals sell the illusion of perfect moments. The infection sells the memory of every moment that wasn't. Both promise you can go back.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Georgie, have you been here before?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (nodding) With Penny. She won me the big bear. Then we got lost on the way home. She was so mad at herself. She kept saying she should have held my hand tighter.
An infected carnival worker operates a game booth, throwing balls at targets that never fall. Each miss makes him whisper louder.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: Almost... if I'd just aimed better... if I'd just been better... if I'd just stayed...
You find Penny's prize—the teddy bear, slightly torn, left on a bench. A note in Georgie's handwriting is pinned to it: "For Penny. So she doesn't feel bad anymore. I love you."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (tearing up) I wanted her to stop saying sorry. Now she can't stop. It's all she does.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: We're going to find a way to quiet the regrets. For her. For everyone. You're not alone in this.
The Ferris wheel starts moving on its own. At the top, a figure stands—looking out over the city as if searching for someone who isn't there.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Figure (distant echo)
steps.text: I should have stayed on the ground... with them... I should have said no to the late shift...

options.label: Climb the Ferris wheel for a better view of the city and Mr. P's possible location
Search the prize booths for useful items and more of Georgie's notes
Follow the sound of music toward the main tent
Ask Georgie to tell you more about the day he and Penny got lost

steps.text: Main path: Search booths, find a clue about Mr. P's next location—the Plant.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Mr. P is heading to the old chemical plant. That's where he made the first batches. If we get there, we can stop the source. We can stop the whispers.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Will that bring Penny back? Really back?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: I don't know. But it's the only chance we have. And I won't leave you behind to find out.
Under the carnival lights, hope and regret dance in the same circle.
End of Chapter 8
Scene: Lucella City streets. Cars abandoned mid-traffic. Billboards for Mr. P's "Miracle Cure" still stand, now torn and dripping with rain. Sirens wail in the distance but never arrive.
The city was built on ambition. Now it stands as a monument to every dream deferred. Every street is a path someone meant to take and didn't.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (navigating with Georgie) Stick to the alleys. The main roads are swarming. If anyone starts talking about what they should have done, keep walking.
Groups of infected move in patterns that almost resemble their old routines—commuting, shopping, waiting for buses that will never come.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: I was going to propose today... the ring is still in my pocket...

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Another
steps.text: My daughter's recital... I missed it again... I always miss it...

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (quiet) They sound like my parents. Before they got sick. Always saying they were sorry for working late.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The infection didn't create the regret. It just made it impossible to ignore. Mr. P thought he could control that. He was wrong.

You pass a pharmacy where Mr. P's distribution vans are parked, doors open, empty crates scattered. A map inside one van shows the final delivery point: the chemical plant on the edge of the industrial district.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: He's not trying to cure them anymore. He's trying to erase the regrets. Or drown in them. Either way, we have to reach the Plant before he finishes whatever he's building.

options.label: Search the vans for more samples or notes
Move quickly through the city toward the industrial district
Try to help a small group of infected who seem less aggressive
Leave a message for other survivors using the pharmacy's radio

steps.text: Main path: Gather what you can and keep moving.
Above the city of unfinished lives, two figures walk toward the source of every echo.
End of Chapter 9
Scene: Lucella Shopping Mall. Escalators frozen. Mannequins stand in shop windows, some now infected and twitching. The food court is a battlefield of overturned tables. Georgie recognizes a store.
Malls promise everything you could want. The infection reminds you of everything you already lost. Both are full of things people meant to buy and never did.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Penny and I came here for bracelets once. Matching ones. She said if we got lost, we could find each other by the color.

You find the jewelry store. Most of the cases are smashed, but one display remains intact—two simple bracelets, one red, one blue. A note is taped to the glass in Mr. P's handwriting: "For those who want to remember only the good years. Final batch."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: He's still distributing. Even now.
An infected shopper stands in front of a mannequin, adjusting its scarf over and over.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Shopper
steps.text: I should have bought it for her... she asked so many times...

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (putting on the blue bracelet) When we find Penny, I'll give her the red one. So she knows I don't regret being her brother. So she can stop saying sorry.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: That's the best cure I've heard all day.

options.label: Take the bracelets and essential supplies
Sabotage the mall's power to slow any pursuit
Leave a message for other survivors
Search the security office for camera footage of Mr. P

steps.text: Main path: Take supplies and bracelets, then exit toward the Plant.
In the temple of want, a small act of remembrance becomes resistance.
End of Chapter 10
Scene: Military outpost on the edge of the city. Barricades of sandbags and vehicles. A few uninfected soldiers remain, exhausted. Radios buzz with desperate calls. Georgie stays close to the Player.
Even soldiers carry regrets—orders followed, lives not saved, families left behind. The infection has reached them too.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: You made it through the city? With a kid? Impressive. Or stupid. Either way, you're here.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: We're heading to the Plant. Mr. P is there. He's the source. He created the potion and he won't stop.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: We know. We've been trying to contain it. But every time we "neutralize" one, they whisper something that makes the next shot harder. "I was going to call my mom." "I never told her I loved her." "I should have come home."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (quietly) They remember too. Just like Penny.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Yeah. Command wants us to burn the Plant. But if there's a real cure in there... we need it. Half my unit is already turning. They're locking themselves in cells so they don't hurt anyone. They're still saying sorry through the doors.
You meet a scientist who escaped the Plant earlier. Her hands shake as she speaks.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Scientist
steps.text: Mr. P's latest formula doesn't just infect. It forces the host to relive their deepest regret on loop. He thinks if he can perfect it, he can make his wife "remember" only their happy years. But it's destroying him. He's talking to her constantly now. Even when she's not there.

options.label: Request military escort to the Plant
Take whatever anti-infection gear they have and go alone with Georgie
Help secure the outpost first
Ask the scientist for any notes on a possible neutralizer

steps.text: Main path: Take gear—gas masks, a sample of potential neutralizer—and proceed with Georgie.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: If I don't come back, get this kid to safety. His name is Georgie. His sister is Penny. They both deserve better than this. Tell them I tried.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: We'll try. Good luck. And... if you see any of my people in there... tell them it's not their fault. Tell them they can stop saying sorry.
At the edge of order, one more promise is made against the tide of regret.
End of Chapter 11

Scene: The chemical plant. Vats of red liquid bubble. Pipes hiss. Mr. P stands at the central console, lab coat stained, talking to an empty space beside him. Georgie and the Player step into the light.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (softly) You always hated the smell of the lab. I should have worked from home. I should have been there when the pain started. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. I can fix it. I just need a little more time.
Here, at the heart of the outbreak, the first regret still speaks. And it has never stopped.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (stepping forward, Georgie behind) Mr. P. It's over. Stop the production. The potion doesn't save anyone. It chains them.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (turning, eyes flickering between normal and crimson) Player. You don't understand. I can fix it. I can make the memories kind again. My wife... she doesn't have to suffer the "what ifs" anymore. None of them do. If I can just adjust the formula one more time—

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: But they can't stop saying sorry! Penny keeps saying she's sorry she got lost! I don't want her to be sorry. I want her to be my sister! I want her to come home!

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (looking at Georgie, recognition dawning) You're the boy. From the house. Your sister... she was one of the first after my wife. She fought it. Kept saying your name. Even when she couldn't see you anymore.
Infected workers begin to close in, but slowly, as if reluctant. Some of them stop when they hear Georgie's voice.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The potion doesn't erase regret. It chains people to it. You're not saving anyone. You're trapping them in the worst moment of their lives. Your wife didn't want this. She told you to live.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (voice cracking) Then what do I do? Let her go? Let all of them go? I can't. I won't regret not trying. I won't be the man who gave up.

options.label: Destroy the main vat
Try to reason and offer the neutralizer sample
Confront him with Mrs. P's recording
Let Georgie speak to him

steps.text: Main path: Play the recording and offer a different path.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (playing the recording) Listen. She already told you what she wanted.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mrs. P (recording)
steps.text: ...don't blame yourself. Live. For both of us. Don't spend the rest of your life saying sorry to a ghost.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (falling to his knees) She... she said that? She really said that?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: She didn't want this. None of them do. Help me shut it down. Help me find a way to let them rest—or remember without the chains. You can still choose something else.
Mr. P stares at the console for a long moment. Then, with shaking hands, he begins the shutdown sequence. The red glow in the vats begins to fade.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (whispering) I'm sorry. To all of you. And to you, my love. I'll try to live. I'll try.
The vats power down. Across the city, the infected pause. Some collapse. Some simply... stop whispering. For the first time in weeks, the air is quiet.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (running to a nearby figure) Penny?
Penny stands there, eyes clearing, though tears remain. She looks at Georgie, then at the bracelet in his hand.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (hoarse) Georgie...? I... I was so scared I lost you. I'm sorry. I'm so—

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (hugging her, holding out the bracelet) Don't be sorry. Just be here. I don't regret you. I never did.
Not every regret vanishes. But some can be answered. Some can be met with something stronger than an apology.
End of Chapter 12

Scene: Weeks later. The Piggy Residence, cleaned but still scarred. Morning light through repaired windows. Georgie and Penny sit on the porch. The Player stands nearby, Doggy's old badge in hand. The city is quieter now.

The outbreak ended, but the echoes did not. Some infected recovered enough to speak their regrets aloud and then let them go. Others remained changed, carrying quieter versions of who they were. The city began to rebuild—not by forgetting, but by choosing what to carry forward.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (looking at her bracelet) I still hear it sometimes. The "what if I had held his hand tighter." But then I look at him, and it's quieter. He won't let me say sorry for being his sister.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Player comes by every week. Says the station is open again. Doggy... he didn't make it all the way back. But he left a note. "Don't hesitate to live." We put it on the wall.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (joining them) Mr. P is helping the scientists. He's not the same. None of us are. But he's trying to make something that eases the memories instead of sharpening them. He listens to the recording every morning.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Will it work?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: I don't know. But for the first time, the question isn't only about what we regret. It's about what we do next. And who we choose to stay with while we figure it out.
A breeze moves through the trees. Somewhere in the distance, a Ferris wheel turns slowly, lights off, waiting for someone to climb it again.
In Lucella, the regrets remain—as they always will. But they no longer rule. They are simply part of the story. And stories, unlike potions, can be rewritten by the ones who keep living them.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: Thank you for playing *Echoes of Regret*. Your choices shaped the memories that remain. The story continues in every life that chooses to answer its echoes instead of being defined by them.
THE END

chapters.title: EXTENDED INTERLUDE: THE WEIGHT OF MEMORY

steps.text: Scene: Between the chapters, time bends. The infection does not only infect the body; it infects the timeline of regret. The Player finds themselves in a place that is neither past nor present—a corridor of locked doors, each one labeled with a name and a date.
Every choice leaves an echo. Every path not taken becomes a room the infected cannot leave. Here, in the space between the House and the Plant, the weight of every "what if" gathers like fog.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: You have entered the Memory Corridor. Some doors open to scenes that never happened. Some open to scenes that still could.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (touching a door labeled "Doggy - Midnight") What is this place?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Voice (unseen, familiar)
steps.text: The place where regrets go when they are too heavy to carry alone. Open a door. Or walk past them all. The story continues either way.

options.label: Open the door marked Doggy
Open the door marked Mrs. P
Open the door marked Georgie and Penny
Walk the full length of the corridor without opening anything

steps.text: Main path continues below. All paths reconverge.
Door: Doggy

The door opens onto a quiet apartment at midnight. A woman sits on a couch, phone in hand, waiting. The clock reads 12:07. A key turns in the lock. Doggy steps inside, still in uniform, badge gleaming. He is not infected. This is the night that did not happen.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: (smiling, tired) Told you I'd be back by midnight. Traffic was nothing. The station was quiet for once.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Partner
steps.text: (standing, relief in every line of her body) You always say that. One day you're going to be late and I'm going to worry myself sick.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: (pulling her close) Then I'll just have to never be late again. Come on. Let's eat. I brought those noodles you like from the place on 5th.
They move to the kitchen. The lights are warm. No rain. No red eyes. For one stolen night, the promise is kept.
In the corridor, the Player watches through the doorway. The scene does not last. The clock jumps. The rain begins. The badge on the table is the only thing that remains.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (softly) He tried.
Door: Mrs. P
A hospital room. Sunlight. Mrs. P sits up in bed, color in her cheeks for the first time in weeks. Mr. P stands beside her, no lab coat, just a man holding her hand.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mrs. P
steps.text: The doctors say the new treatment is working. You don't have to stay so late anymore. Come home.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (voice thick) I will. I promise. No more nights in the lab. No more potions. Just us.
She smiles. The monitors beep steadily. Outside, the city is whole.
This is the ending Mr. P wrote in his head every night before he poured the next vial. It never left the page.
Door: Georgie and Penny
The Piggy Residence. Afternoon. Penny ties a bracelet around Georgie's wrist. It is blue and red, the colors of his favorite team.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: There. Now you can't get lost. If you wander off, the bracelet will lead you back to me. Always.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (grinning) I'm not going to wander off. I'm staying right here. Race you to the treehouse?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: You're on. And no cheating this time!
They run. Laughter fills the yard. The front door is open. No one is missing.
Some regrets are small. Some are the size of a little brother's hand slipping out of reach. Both can fill a house.

The corridor stretches on. More doors. More nights that never came. The Player steps back into the rain of the real Lucella, the weight of every unopened door settling on their shoulders like a second uniform.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: The echoes are longer than any single night. The story is not finished simply because the last chapter has been written. It continues in every door that remains closed—and in every one that someone finally opens.
To be continued in the living.

Scene: Three months after the plant. The Lucella Police Station has been cleaned. New windows. Fresh paint over the old claw marks. The Player stands at the front desk where Doggy once stood. Georgie and Penny visit after school. The city is quieter, but not silent.
Rebuilding is slower than destruction. Every board replaced is a choice not to let the regret stay in the walls.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (looking around) It doesn't smell like the bad night anymore. It smells like new paper and coffee.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (quietly) Doggy's badge is on the wall. Next to the note. I read it every time we come. "Don't hesitate to live." I think he meant it for all of us.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (setting down a folder of recovered reports) Mr. P sent these over. Notes on the neutralizer trials. Some of the early infected are starting to remember their names without the pain. Not all of them. But some.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Will Penny stop hearing the sorry-voice?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (touching her bracelet) Some days it's loud. Some days it's just a whisper. When Georgie holds my hand, it gets quieter. That's enough for now.
A radio crackles on the desk. Not an emergency. Just the weather. Clear skies over Lucella for the first time in weeks.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: There's still work. The outpost wants a liaison. The school needs someone to talk to the kids who saw too much. And somewhere out there, more people are still walking around inside their worst night. We don't have to save all of them. We just have to keep answering the ones who call.

options.label: Accept the liaison role at the outpost
Spend the afternoon at the school with Georgie and Penny
Visit Mr. P in the lab and ask about the new formula
Walk the old routes alone and listen for remaining echoes

steps.text: Whatever path is chosen, the station remains open. The badge stays on the wall.
The story does not end when the last infected falls or the last vat is emptied. It ends—or continues—when the people who survived decide what they will carry, and what they will set down.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: The full story of Echoes of Regret has been written. Its chapters live in the folder. Its echoes live in the choices still being made.
THE END (and the beginning of what comes after)

chapters.title: FULL EXPANDED SCENE: THE NIGHT BEFORE THE HOUSE

steps.text: Scene: The Piggy Residence, two days before the outbreak reaches the street. Evening. Penny is in the kitchen packing Georgie's lunch for the next day. Georgie sits at the table drawing. Their parents are in the living room, voices low. Outside, the first infected have not yet appeared, but the news is already talking about "isolated cases" and "strange behavior" at the hospital.
Every story has a night before. A last ordinary evening that will later be remembered as the moment everything was still possible.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (calling) Georgie, did you finish your math? Mom said if it's not done you can't watch the show after dinner.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (without looking up) Almost! I'm drawing the treehouse first. See? I put you in it. You're the one with the long hair.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (smiling, coming over) That's not me. That's you with long hair. You always do that.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (giggling) No, look—see the bracelet? I drew the bracelet. That means it's you.
He holds up the paper. Crayon lines. A small figure with a red-and-blue bracelet standing on a platform of sticks. Next to him, a taller figure with no bracelet, arms open.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (soft) It's good. Really good. Put it on the fridge so Mom and Dad can see it.
She pins it up. From the living room, their mother's voice rises slightly, then falls.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mother (distant)
steps.text: We should keep him home tomorrow. Just in case. The school sent that letter about the hospital cases.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Father (distant)
steps.text: It's three blocks away. And they said it was contained. If we keep him home every time the news says something, he'll never go anywhere.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mother
steps.text: I just have a feeling. Like the house is already too quiet. Like something's listening.
Regret does not always announce itself with screams. Sometimes it begins as a feeling in a mother's chest on an ordinary Tuesday night.
Penny returns to the kitchen. She opens a drawer and takes out the bracelet—real this time, not crayon. She turns it over in her hands.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (to herself) If I give it to him tonight, he'll wear it tomorrow. Then if anything happens... he'll have it. He'll know I'm looking for him.
She walks back to the table. Georgie is still drawing, tongue between his teeth in concentration.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Hey. Close your eyes.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Why?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Just do it. Trust me.
He does. She ties the bracelet around his wrist, carefully, not too tight.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (opening his eyes) It's the real one! The one from the carnival last year! You said I couldn't have it until I was older!

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: You're old enough tonight. Promise me something. If you ever get lost—if anything ever feels wrong—you look at this. And you remember I'm coming to find you. No matter what. Okay?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (serious for once) Okay. I promise. But I'm not gonna get lost. I'm staying right here.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (hugging him) I know. Just... promise anyway.
From the living room, the television volume rises. A news anchor's calm voice. The word "outbreak" is used for the first time on the local channel. Neither child hears it clearly. Their parents do.

In two days the house will be dark. The drawings will still be on the fridge. The bracelet will be the only thing Georgie has left when he runs. And Penny will spend every moment after saying the word "sorry" to a little brother who cannot hear her anymore.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: This is the night the story almost didn't need to happen. It happened anyway.

Scene: The Lucella Mall, six months after the outbreak. Most stores are boarded. A few have reopened with limited hours. The food court is half-empty. The Player walks through with Georgie and Penny. They came for school supplies. The escalators are running again. Somewhere, an old carnival jingle plays from a broken speaker in the arcade.

Places remember too. The mall remembers the night the lights went out and the infected walked the corridors looking for the people they had lost. Some of those people are still here—working, shopping, trying to be ordinary again.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (pointing) That's the store where we got the bracelet. The one that closed. They have a new sign now. "Open for survivors." That's a weird sign.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (quiet) A lot of signs are weird now. At least they're open.

An infected woman stands near the fountain. She is not aggressive. She is simply standing, hands open, whispering to the water. Her eyes are still faintly red at the edges. A recovery bracelet—new design, blue instead of the old red—circles her wrist.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Woman
steps.text: (soft) I told him I'd meet him by the fountain at six. I was late. The line at the bakery was long. I was only ten minutes late. He wasn't there. He wasn't anywhere. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry I was late.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (approaching carefully) Ma'am? The outbreak is over. The fountain is just a fountain now. You don't have to wait here.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Woman
steps.text: (looking up, recognition flickering) Is he coming? My son. He was six. He had a red hat. I bought him the hat here. At the store with the balloons. He loved balloons.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (stepping forward, voice gentle) Maybe he's waiting somewhere else. Maybe he's waiting for you to stop saying sorry and go look for him instead.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Woman
steps.text: (tears, the red in her eyes dimming) I don't know how to stop. Every time I try to walk away, I hear him calling. "Mom, where are you?" And I have to answer. I have to say I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (holding up his own bracelet) My sister gave me this so I wouldn't get lost. She found me anyway. Even when I was really lost. Maybe your son is looking for you too. But he can't find you if you stay by the fountain forever.
The woman stares at the bracelet. Her hands lower. For the first time, she steps back from the water.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Woman
steps.text: (whispering) If I leave... and he's not there... what do I do with the sorry?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: You carry it. Like the rest of us. And you keep walking until you find something louder than the apology.
She nods, slowly. She turns. She walks toward the exit. The red in her eyes is still there, but it is no longer the only color.
Not every recovery is a cure. Some are simply the decision to stop standing in the same place and calling the same name into empty air.

options.label: Follow the woman to make sure she reaches the exit safely
Stay with Georgie and Penny and finish the school supply run
Check the arcade for more lingering infected who might still be reachable
Call the recovery team and report the woman's location

steps.text: Main path: The group continues. The woman is seen later, outside, looking at the sky instead of the fountain.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (after a long silence) Do you think she finds him?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: I don't know. But she left the fountain. That's more than a lot of people manage.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: If she doesn't find him, maybe she can find someone else who needs a mom. There's a lot of kids at school who don't have anyone left. Mrs. Henderson says some of them still wait by the doors at the end of the day.

The mall remembers the night everything broke. It also remembers the afternoon a woman finally walked away from a fountain and a little boy suggested that waiting was not the only kind of love left in the world.
End of Chapter 14

chapters.title: THE LONG ROAD: SCENES FROM THE YEAR AFTER

steps.text: A year passes. The city of Lucella does not return to what it was. It becomes something that knows the shape of its own scars. The following scenes are not chapters in the old sense. They are the ordinary days that follow the extraordinary night. They are the story continuing because the people in it refused to let the last page be the end.
Scene: The School Reopens

Lucella Elementary. New locks on the doors. A counselor in every hallway for the first month. Georgie sits at his old desk. The drawing of the treehouse is still taped inside his notebook. Penny waits for him outside after the final bell, bracelet visible on her wrist.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Teacher
steps.text: (to the class) Today we are writing about something we are glad we still have. It can be a person. A place. A thing. It does not have to be perfect. It only has to be true.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (writing slowly) I am glad I still have my sister. She found me when I was lost. She still finds me when the sorry-voice gets loud. I am glad the bracelet is real.
After class, he shows Penny the paper. She reads it twice.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (voice thick) I'm glad I still have you too. Even on the days I hear myself saying sorry for things that already happened. Especially on those days.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Then don't say it. Just be here. That's what the Player said. That's what Doggy's note said. Don't hesitate to live.
They walk home together. The path is longer than it used to be because some streets are still closed. They take the long way on purpose. It gives them more time.
Scene: Mr. P's New Laboratory

A smaller room now. No bubbling red vats. Glass jars of clear liquid. Recordings of recovered patients playing softly in the background. Mr. P sits with headphones on, listening to his wife's voice from the old message. The Player knocks and enters.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (removing the headphones) The neutralizer is stable. We gave it to twelve volunteers this week. Nine of them reported the regrets becoming... quieter. Not gone. Quieter. Like a radio turned down instead of a scream in the same room.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: And the other three?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: Still loud. One of them asked to stop the trial. Said the quiet felt worse than the noise because at least the noise proved the person they lost had been real. I don't have an answer for that yet.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: You don't have to have all the answers. You just have to keep trying something that doesn't chain people to the worst night of their lives.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (looking at the empty chair beside him) She would have liked that. The trying. She always said I spent too much time looking for the perfect formula and not enough time sitting in the imperfect room with her.
He presses play on the recording again. Mrs. P's voice fills the small lab: "Don't stay so late again, love. The house is too quiet without you."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (soft) I'm not staying late tonight. I'm going home. Even if the house is still quiet. Even if I have to sit in the quiet on purpose.
Scene: The Carnival Lights

The old carnival grounds. The Ferris wheel has been repaired. It turns slowly, lights on for the first time in over a year. A small crowd has gathered. Not many. Enough. Georgie and Penny stand in line. The Player is with them, Doggy's badge clipped to their belt.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Do you think Doggy would have ridden it?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: He would have complained about the height the whole way up. Then he would have smiled at the top and pretended he hadn't been scared.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (looking at the lights) I used to be scared of heights. After the outbreak I was scared of everything else more. Heights don't seem so bad now.
They board. The wheel lifts them above the city. Lucella spreads out below—some streets dark, some bright, all of them still standing.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (pointing) There's the house. There's the school. There's the mall. There's the station. We're higher than all of them.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (leaning on the rail) And we're still here. All three of us. That's the part that matters.

From the top of the wheel, the regrets of the city are still visible. They are also smaller. Distance does that. So does time. So does the choice to keep climbing even when the ground below is full of things that hurt.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: The story of Echoes of Regret is no longer only the story of the outbreak. It is the story of the year that followed, and the years that will follow that. It is finished in the sense that the first book has been written. It is unfinished in the sense that every person who survived is still writing their own next page.
THE END OF THE FIRST BOOK
THE BEGINNING OF EVERYTHING AFTER

chapters.title: BOOK TWO: THE WEIGHT OF QUIET

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: Book One complete. Book Two begins. The infection is quieter. The regrets are not.

Scene: Lucella Police Station, one year later. Boards have been removed from most windows. The fluorescent lights still buzz, but some bulbs have been replaced. A new sign hangs above the front desk: "Recovery Desk — Speak First." Doggy's old badge is mounted in a glass case. The Player stands behind the counter now, wearing a different uniform. Georgie sits in a chair nearby, drawing. Penny stands by the window, watching the street.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (not looking up) Mrs. Henderson says the school counselor wants to talk to me again. About the treehouse. About the night.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: You don't have to go if you don't want to.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I know. I just don't like when they ask if I still hear her voice. I do. But it's not the bad voice anymore. It's just... her. The one who used to read to me.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (quietly) Sometimes I still hear myself yelling. In the house. Before everything. I don't know how to make that stop.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: You don't make it stop. You make something else louder. That's what we've been doing.
A radio crackles. A new report from the outskirts. Someone found an old vial of the original potion. Red. Still sealed.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Recovery team requesting backup. Old lab site. Possible residual activation. Over.

options.label: Go with the recovery team yourself
Send Penny and stay with Georgie
Ask Mr. P to join the team
Monitor from the station and prepare the neutralizer

steps.text: Main path: The Player goes. Penny insists on coming. Georgie stays with a trusted officer.
The station remembers the night Doggy turned. It also remembers the morning the boards came down. Both memories stay. One does not cancel the other.
End of Chapter 15 opening
CHAPTER 15 CONTINUED: THE OLD LAB

Scene: The ruins of Mr. P's original laboratory annex. Half the roof is gone. Rain falls through the gaps. Glass vials, long empty, lie cracked on the floor. A sealed red vial sits on a metal table, still glowing faintly. Three recovery team members stand back. One of them is an infected who has not fully recovered—eyes half-red, hands shaking.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Recovery Lead
steps.text: We haven't touched it. Orders were to wait for you.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Good. Don't. That liquid doesn't just infect the body. It feeds on the last thing you wished you could undo.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (staring at the vial) It looks like the color of the night I lost him. The first night. Before the bat. Before the house.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Penny. Look at me, not the vial.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: I'm looking. I just... I remember the exact sound of my voice when I told him to go to his room. I remember thinking it was the right thing. I was wrong. The potion would have made me live inside that wrong forever.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Infected Team Member
steps.text: (whispering) Mine is the day I didn't call my mother back. She left a message. I was busy. The red made me hear the message on a loop. For months. Even after the neutralizer, I still hear the end of it. "Call me when you can."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: We're not opening the vial. We're destroying it. Properly. Mr. P developed a method.
You carefully place the vial inside a containment case. As the lid seals, the faint glow dims.

Some regrets cannot be burned. They can only be sealed and carried somewhere they cannot spread. The Player knows this. So does Penny. The difference is that they have learned to walk while carrying them.

options.label: Destroy the vial on site with the neutralizer compound
Take it back to Mr. P's new lab for study
Bury it deep in the forest where no one will find it
Ask the infected team member what they need before deciding

steps.text: Main path: Take it to Mr. P. He needs to see it to confirm the formula is fully neutralized in the wild.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (as you leave) Do you ever wonder if we should have just left all of them sealed? The old labs. The old houses. The old nights.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: No. Because Georgie is still drawing pictures of the treehouse. And you're still here to look at them. Sealing everything would have sealed him too.
End of Chapter 15

Scene: Lucella Mall, central fountain. The water runs clear now. No red tint. A few recovered people sit on the edges. The woman from a year ago is not there. A new person sits alone—a man in a faded carnival worker vest. He stares at the water.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: (not looking up) I used to run the Ferris wheel. The night it stopped, a kid got scared halfway up. I told him to stay in the car. I went down to check the motor. When I came back... the cars were empty. The infection had reached the grounds. I never found the kid. I still hear him calling for his mom from the top.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The wheel runs again. People ride it.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: I know. I watched from outside last month. I couldn't go in. What if I hear him again? What if the sound is real this time and I still can't reach him?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Then you walk toward the sound instead of away from it. That's the only thing that worked for me. Running made the voice louder. Standing still made it louder. Walking made it... smaller. Not gone. Smaller.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: (finally looking up, eyes mostly clear) Did it work?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: I'm still walking. My brother is still here. That's as close to "worked" as we get.

options.label: Offer to ride the Ferris wheel with him
Sit with him until he decides to leave on his own
Tell him about Doggy's note
Leave him the location of the recovery counselor

steps.text: Main path: Sit with him. After twenty minutes he stands. He does not ride the wheel. He walks out of the mall. The next day the recovery team reports he checked in voluntarily.
Not every person who sits at the fountain leaves healed. Some leave walking. That is enough for the story to continue.
End of Chapter 16

Scene: The backyard of the old Piggy house. The house itself is boarded and marked for demolition, but the treehouse remains. Georgie climbs the ladder carefully. The Player and Penny wait below. A new rope ladder has been added. Inside the treehouse, old drawings are still taped to the walls. One shows a family of four. The faces have been redrawn so many times the paper is thin.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (calling down) The drawing is still here. The one I made before. The one with all of us.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Can I come up?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Yeah. But only if you don't say sorry when you see it.
Penny climbs. The treehouse creaks but holds. She sits across from Georgie. The Player stays below, listening.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (pointing) That's you. That's me. That's Mom. That's Dad. I drew Dad even though he wasn't home much. I wanted him in the picture anyway.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (voice careful) I used to think if I just said the right sorry, the picture would go back to normal. It doesn't work like that.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I know. Mrs. Henderson says pictures don't fix things. People do. Or they don't. But we can still look at the picture.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (from below) You two okay up there?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: We're okay. We're just looking.

The treehouse does not erase the night the house filled with red light. It simply remains. Georgie remains. Penny remains. The Player remains on the ground, ready if the ladder breaks. That is the shape of the story now.

options.label: Climb up and look at the drawing with them
Stay below and keep watch
Suggest taking the drawing back to the new apartment
Ask Georgie if he wants to rebuild the treehouse somewhere safer

steps.text: Main path: The Player climbs up. The three of them sit in the small space. No one speaks for a long time. When they climb down, Georgie carries the drawing. He does not fold it.
End of Chapter 17

chapters.title: CHAPTER 18: MR. P AND THE EMPTY CHAIR

steps.text: Scene: Mr. P's new laboratory. Smaller. Cleaner. The empty chair still sits beside his desk. A fresh recording of Mrs. P plays at low volume. The Player enters with the containment case from the old lab.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: You found one. Intact.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Sealed. We didn't open it. Penny was with me. She didn't look away.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (taking the case carefully) Good. The formula is stable enough now that exposure shouldn't trigger full regression if the person has already had the neutralizer. Still. Better not to test it.
He places the case in a locked cabinet. Then he sits. The empty chair is still empty.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: She recorded that message the week before she got sick. I used to play it to remember her voice. Then I played it because the potion made me hear it wrong. Now I play it because I choose to. The difference is small. It still matters.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Are you going home tonight?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: I am. The house is still quiet. I bought a second chair for the kitchen. I don't sit in it. I just... have it. In case.

Mr. P does not get his wife back. No one in Lucella gets the exact thing they lost returned unchanged. What they get is the chance to sit in a room that is no longer only filled with the sound of what they cannot fix.

options.label: Ask to hear the full recording
Leave him to go home
Offer to sit in the second chair for a while
Ask about the next batch of neutralizer

steps.text: Main path: The Player sits in the second chair. They do not speak. The recording ends. Mr. P turns it off. They leave the lab together. The second chair stays.
End of Chapter 18

Scene: Carnival grounds after closing. The Ferris wheel is still. Lights are off except for the maintenance lamps. The man from the mall fountain is there, wearing his old vest. He stands at the base of the wheel, looking up.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: I came back. I don't know why. The kid's not here. I know that. But the sound... it was so clear for so long. I thought if I stood in the same place, maybe I could answer him this time.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Did you?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: No. The sound isn't here. It's just in me. Standing here doesn't make it louder. It also doesn't make it go away. It just... is.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (arriving with Georgie, who insisted on coming) We brought the drawing. Georgie wanted to show you something.
Georgie holds up a new drawing. It shows the Ferris wheel. A small figure stands at the bottom. Another small figure is at the top, waving. Both figures are smiling.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I drew him waving. Not calling. Just waving. In case that helps.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: (taking the drawing carefully) It does. Thank you. I don't know if I'll hang it up. But I'll keep it.

The carnival remembers the night the cars emptied. It also remembers the night a man stood under a dark wheel and accepted a drawing of a wave instead of a call. Both nights stay. The man walks home with the paper folded once, not crumpled.

options.label: Stay until he leaves
Help him lock up the grounds
Ask if he wants to ride the wheel tomorrow when it opens
Leave the drawing and go

steps.text: Main path: They help him lock the gates. He thanks them. He does not ride the wheel the next day. He does hang the drawing in his apartment. The recovery counselor notes the change.
End of Chapter 19

Scene: A storage room beneath the new hospital. Shelves of containment cases. Most are empty. One remains. The last known intact sample of the original red potion. Mr. P, the Player, Penny, and a small recovery team stand in front of it.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: This is the last one we know of. After this, any remaining samples are either destroyed or too degraded to activate. If we neutralize this one, the original formula ends here.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: And if we keep it?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: Then someone, someday, might open it because they think they can control what it does. They will be wrong. The potion does not care about control. It only cares about the last thing you cannot forgive yourself for.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Then we end it. Not because it fixes anything. Because it stops the next person from having to learn the same lesson the hard way.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (who was not supposed to be there but followed) Can I watch? I want to see it stop.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: You can watch. You don't have to.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I want to.
Mr. P opens the containment case. He pours the neutralizer compound over the vial. The red liquid inside turns clear, then cloudy, then still. The glow dies.

The last vial does not explode. It does not scream. It simply stops being red. Somewhere in the city, a person who has been hearing the same apology for a year hears it one less time. They do not know why. They only know the room is slightly quieter.

options.label: Destroy the empty vial as well
Keep the neutralized sample for records
Ask Georgie how he feels
Leave the storage room and lock it

steps.text: Main path: They destroy the vial. Georgie watches. He does not cry. He asks if they can go get ice cream after. They do.
End of Chapter 20

Scene: The new apartment where Penny and Georgie live now. Smaller than the old house. Two bedrooms. A kitchen table with three chairs. The drawing from the treehouse is framed on the wall. The Player is visiting. Rain taps the window, the same sound as the night everything started, but softer.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (setting the table) Mrs. Henderson says I can stop seeing the counselor if I want. I told her I might keep going. Not because I have to. Because sometimes I like having someone to tell the treehouse story to who wasn't there.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (pouring water) I still say sorry sometimes. In my head. For the yelling. For the bat. For not finding you faster. It doesn't stop. It just doesn't run the whole house anymore.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: That's the difference the neutralizer couldn't make. Only time and choosing to stay could.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Are you staying for dinner?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: If you want me to.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I want you to. We have an extra chair.
They eat. The rain continues. No one mentions the old house. No one needs to. The framed drawing is enough.

The story does not end with a cure. It ends with a table that has three chairs and people who sit in them on purpose. The regrets are still in the room. They are no longer the only thing in the room. That is the finished shape of *Echoes of Regret*.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: Book Two complete. The full story of PIGGY: ECHOES OF REGRET has reached its ending. The city of Lucella continues. The people in it continue. The writing stops here.
THE END

chapters.title: BOOK THREE: THE ECHOES THAT REMAIN

steps.text: Continuing the Visual Novel - Years After the Quiet House

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: The table has three chairs. The city has quieted. But echoes do not vanish when the last chapter ends. They wait in the corners of ordinary days. Book Three begins when the ordinary starts to remember again.

Two years after the night the rain stopped being only rain, Lucella has rebuilt most of its streets. The plant is sealed. The carnival runs again in summer. The station keeps Doggy's badge on the wall. Penny and Georgie go to school. The Player still answers calls that sound too much like the old ones. Mr. P still keeps the second chair empty. The story continues because people do.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 22: THE CALL THAT SOUNDED LIKE BEFORE

steps.text: Scene: Lucella Police Station, late afternoon. Fluorescent lights. The Player is at the desk filling out a report about a missing dog when the radio crackles with a familiar static.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Unit 4, respond to 14 Maple Street. Neighbor reports screaming. Child involved. Possible... (static) ...regret pattern.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (freezing, pen still) Say again. Maple Street?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Confirmed. 14 Maple. Be advised, subject may still be verbal.
Maple Street is two blocks from the old Piggy house. The boarded windows are still there. The treehouse is gone now. Georgie took the drawings when they moved.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (internal) It can't be starting again. The neutralizer was distributed. The last sealed vials were destroyed. We checked.
You grab the keys. The new car starts on the first try. On the way, you call Penny.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Stay inside. Both of you. I'm checking something. Don't open the door for anyone until I call back.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (voice tight) Is it... is it red again?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: I don't know yet. Just stay.

options.label: Drive straight to Maple Street with lights on
Stop at the old house first to check the boards
Call Mr. P on the way and ask if any samples are missing
Tell dispatch to send backup and wait

steps.text: Main path: You drive to Maple Street. The house looks ordinary. A woman stands on the porch in a bathrobe, holding a phone. She is crying but her eyes are clear.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Woman
steps.text: It's my husband. He came home from work and started talking to someone who wasn't there. He keeps saying "I'm sorry I didn't answer when you called." Our son is upstairs. He locked himself in the bathroom. Please. He's not violent. He just... won't stop apologizing to the empty chair.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (stepping carefully inside) Sir? Police. Can you hear me?
The man sits at the kitchen table. An empty chair across from him. He looks up. His eyes are red from crying, not from infection.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: She called. From the hospital. The night she died. I was in the garage. I didn't hear the phone. I've been saying it for three years. Tonight it just... got louder. Like someone turned the volume up on the whole house.
Not the potion. Not the red. Just a man who has been carrying the same sentence for three years, and a night when the sentence decided to fill the room again.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (quietly) The volume can be turned down. It takes more than one night. But it can.

You sit in the empty chair. You do not speak for a long time. The man stops repeating the sentence. He starts to cry differently. The son comes downstairs. No one is infected. The call is still answered.
End of Chapter 22
Scene: Lucella Elementary, after school. Art room. Georgie is nine now. He stays late to finish a project. Penny waits in the hallway, reading. The Player stops by on the way back from Maple Street.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (holding up a paper) Look. I drew the station. With the badge. And the three chairs. I put the empty one too, but I drew a coat on it so it doesn't look lonely.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: That's good. Mrs. Henderson would like that.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: She said I can draw whatever I want as long as I tell her what it means. This one means the station is still open. Even if Doggy isn't there. The badge is.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (from the doorway) Ready? Mom's making the pasta you like.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Almost. I want to add the treehouse. Even though it's gone. In the corner. Small. So we remember it was real.
He draws a small platform in the background. A figure with a bracelet stands on it, waving.
Georgie does not draw the red. He draws the things that stayed after the red left. The drawing is not a cure. It is a record of what was chosen instead.

options.label: Ask Georgie if he wants to show the drawing to Mr. P
Help him add the music box that still plays sometimes
Tell him about the man on Maple Street without the details
Just watch him finish and walk them both home

steps.text: Main path: You watch. He finishes. The three of you walk home. The drawing stays in his backpack. Later it will go on the fridge. The extra chair at the table will have a place for it to lean against.
End of Chapter 23
