Scene: Mr. P's house. Evening. The kitchen has two chairs now. One is pulled out. Mrs. P's recording plays from a small speaker on the counter, volume low. The Player sits in the second chair without being asked.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: You heard about Maple Street.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: He wasn't infected. Just loud. The sentence got loud.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (nodding) The neutralizer stops the potion from making the sentence the only thing a person can say. It does not stop the sentence from existing. I still have mine. "I'm sorry I stayed late." It doesn't run the house. It sits in the chair sometimes. I let it.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Does it get quieter when someone else sits in the other chair?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: Some nights. Not because the sentence changes. Because the room has more than one sound in it.
The recording ends. Neither of them restarts it. They eat leftovers. The second chair remains occupied until the Player leaves. Mr. P does not move it back under the table right away.
The empty chair is no longer only empty. It is sometimes filled by someone who chooses to sit there and listen to a recording that is not their own. That is a different kind of quiet.
End of Chapter 24

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: Book Three has begun. The echoes continue. The writing continues. The chairs remain.

Scene: Lucella Carnival, opening night of the summer season. The Ferris wheel turns slowly. Lights are bright but not harsh. Families walk the midway. The man from the fountain stands near the base of the wheel, not looking up this time. He holds Georgie's drawing in one hand. Penny and Georgie are ahead, buying cotton candy. The Player walks with them.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: I came back. Not to wait. Just to see if the wheel still makes the same sound. It does. The kid isn't calling. The sound is just the wheel. I can hear the difference now.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (running back) Do you want to ride? We have an extra ticket. I asked.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: (looking at the ticket) I don't know if I should. Last time I stood under it for hours.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: You don't have to stand under it. You can sit in a seat. With us. Or not. The ticket is just a ticket.

The carnival does not erase the night the man heard a child calling from the top of a wheel that was not moving. It simply runs again. People choose whether to stand under it or ride it. Both are allowed.

options.label: Ride the Ferris wheel with Georgie, Penny, and the man
Stay on the ground and watch them go up
Ask the man if he wants to keep the drawing or give it back
Walk the midway and listen for any other echoes among the games

steps.text: Main path: They ride. The man sits across from Georgie. Halfway up, the city spreads below them. No one is calling. The man laughs once, short and surprised. When they get off, he folds the drawing carefully and puts it in his pocket. He does not look back at the wheel.
End of Chapter 25

Scene: Lucella Elementary gymnasium. Morning assembly. The principal stands at the podium. Behind her, a screen shows a simple slide: "If you hear someone talking to a person who isn't there, tell a teacher. You are not in trouble. They are not in trouble. We will listen." Georgie sits with his class. Penny is in the row behind, visiting for the assembly because the Player asked her to come.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Principal
steps.text: We have learned that some nights get loud. Not because of monsters. Because of sentences people have been saying for a long time. If a sentence gets too loud in your house, you can tell us. We will sit with you until it gets quieter. That is all.
Some of the younger children fidget. A few of the older ones look at their shoes. Georgie raises his hand.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: What if the sentence is sorry? And the person already said it a lot?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Principal
steps.text: Then we still sit. Sometimes sorry needs company more than it needs another sorry. You don't have to fix it. You just have to stay in the room.

The assembly is not a lesson about the infection. The infection is gone. It is a lesson about the ordinary weight that remains when the extraordinary leaves. Georgie already knows the lesson. He is checking that the adults know it too.

options.label: Speak to the principal afterward about adding a counselor visit to every classroom
Walk Georgie and Penny home and ask what they thought
Visit the art room and look at the drawings on the wall
Call Mr. P and tell him the school is teaching the difference between loud and red

steps.text: Main path: You walk them home. Georgie says the principal got it right. Penny says she might volunteer to help with the younger kids next time. The extra chair at dinner has Georgie's backpack on it until he moves it.
End of Chapter 26

chapters.title: CHAPTER 27: THE LAST VIAL THAT WASN'T

steps.text: Scene: The sealed storage room beneath the old plant. The Player and Mr. P stand outside the locked door. A maintenance worker reported a light on inside. The light is off now. The door is still sealed. The containment case from years ago is empty. Everything was neutralized.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: There is nothing left that can turn red. I checked the inventory twice. The light was probably a sensor. Or a reflection.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Or someone who still thinks a vial can fix the sentence they keep hearing.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: If they break the seal, they will find empty shelves. The potion is gone. The regret is not. They will have to learn the difference the long way.
You both listen. No sound from inside. No heartbeat in a liquid that is no longer there.
The plant does not hold the cure or the curse anymore. It holds the proof that both were once possible. The proof stays sealed. The people who need it already have the quieter version.

options.label: Leave the seal intact and post a new sign
Open the door once to confirm the shelves are empty
Ask Mr. P if he wants to keep a single empty vial for the records
Walk the perimeter and listen for anyone who might return

steps.text: Main path: You leave the seal. You post a sign that says "Empty. The sentence is not inside." Mr. P does not ask to take anything. You drive back to the station. The badge is still on the wall.
End of Chapter 27

Scene: The new apartment. Night. Penny sits on the couch tying and untying the blue-and-red bracelet she once put on Georgie's wrist. Georgie is asleep. The Player is on the phone in the kitchen, finishing a report. Penny speaks softly so she does not wake him.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: I used to think if I never took it off, he couldn't get lost again. Then I thought if I took it off, I was saying I didn't care. Now I just wear it when I want to. Tonight I wanted to.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (coming in, phone down) He still has the drawing with the bracelet on it. He showed me today.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: I know. He puts it on the fridge every morning and takes it down every night so it doesn't get sauce on it. He is careful with the things that stayed.

Penny does not apologize for the night she swung the bat. She has said the words. They are in the room. They are not the only words. The bracelet is not a lock. It is a choice she makes when she wants the color of it against her wrist.

options.label: Sit with her until she decides whether to leave the bracelet on
Ask if she wants to make a new one for Georgie that matches
Tell her about the man at the carnival who kept the drawing
Make tea and let the silence stay soft

steps.text: Main path: You make tea. She leaves the bracelet on. Georgie wakes once, sees it, and goes back to sleep without saying anything. The three chairs are all occupied by morning.
End of Chapter 28

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: The chapters continue. The chairs stay filled when someone chooses to sit. The echoes remain, but they share the room. The writing has not stopped.

Scene: A small park on the edge of Lucella, six months after the old treehouse was taken down. A new platform has been built in a different tree. It is lower. The rope ladder is new. Georgie climbs it without looking down. Penny stands at the bottom holding the framed drawing from the apartment. The Player watches from the bench.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (calling) It doesn't creak the same. That's okay. The old one creaked because it was old. This one is new. We can make it creak later if we want.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Do you want the drawing up there?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Not yet. I want to draw a new one first. Of this tree. With the three of us. You can be on the ground this time if you want. You don't have to climb.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: I'll climb. Just not today. Today I want to see you from down here so I know the ladder holds.

The new treehouse does not replace the old one. It does not erase the night the old house filled with footsteps that were not Georgie's. It is simply a place that exists now, in a park where the city can see it. Georgie draws it because it is real. Penny stays on the ground because she chooses the view. Both are allowed.

options.label: Help Georgie measure the platform so the new drawing is accurate
Sit on the bench and let them decide the height of the ladder
Ask if they want to invite the man from the carnival to see it
Walk the path around the park and listen for any other children calling names

steps.text: Main path: You sit. Georgie finishes the climb. He waves. Penny waves back. The drawing stays in her hands until they walk home. Later it will hang next to the old one. The new treehouse will get its own drawing by the end of the week.
End of Chapter 29

Scene: Lucella Police Station, after midnight. The Player is the only one on duty. The badge on the wall catches the light from the desk lamp. A radio call comes in—quiet, no emergency. Just a woman who wants to know if anyone else has ever heard their dead mother's voice in the kitchen at 2 a.m. and whether that means the potion is back.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (into the radio) The potion is not back. The voice is. You can turn the light on. You can sit at the table. You can call someone who is still alive and ask them to stay on the phone until the voice gets quieter. Do you want me to stay on the line?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Woman
steps.text: (small) Yes. Please. She keeps saying she left the pie in the oven. I know she didn't. The oven is off. But she keeps saying it.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Then we will sit with the pie that is not there until the sentence finishes. I am not going anywhere.

The call lasts forty minutes. The woman cries. Then she laughs once when the Player describes Doggy's badge and the note under it. When she hangs up, the station is quiet again. The badge is still there.

Not every call is Maple Street. Some are just a woman and a pie that was never left in the oven. The station answers both. The difference between red and ordinary is the difference between a sentence that cannot stop and a sentence that can be sat with until it rests.

options.label: Write the call into the night log under "echo, non-infectious"
Call Penny in the morning and tell her the station is still open
Sit with the badge for a while before going home
Leave a note for the day shift about the pie

steps.text: Main path: You write the log. You sit with the badge. You go home when the sun starts to show. The note under the badge still says "Don't hesitate to live." You do not add anything to it. It is already enough.
End of Chapter 30

Scene: The new apartment. Friday night. Georgie has a friend over from school. The friend is named Leo. Leo has never seen the drawing of the treehouse. Georgie shows it to him carefully. Penny makes popcorn in the kitchen. The Player is not there tonight. The extra chair has Leo's backpack on it.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: This is the old treehouse. The one that got taken down. I drew it so we would remember the platform was real. See the bracelet? That's Penny. She still has it.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Leo
steps.text: Did you fall out of it?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: No. I just got lost once. Not from the treehouse. From the house. Penny found me. That's why the bracelet is in the picture.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Leo
steps.text: Cool. Can we draw a new one? With my house in it too?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Yeah. But only if we put the station in the background. The badge has to be there. It's important.

Georgie does not tell Leo about the bat or the red eyes or the night the music box played for a brother who was not in the room. He tells him about the bracelet and the station. Leo does not ask for the rest. They draw. The popcorn is ready. The sleepover continues. The old story is not the only story in the apartment tonight.

options.label: The scene continues without the Player; they find out in the morning
Penny calls the Player to say the sleepover is going well
Georgie asks Penny if she wants to add herself to the new drawing
They all three sit at the table and the extra chair is just a chair

steps.text: Main path: Penny does not call. In the morning Georgie shows the Player the new drawing. The station is in the background. The badge is a small gold square. Leo's house is next to the treehouse. No one is missing from the picture. The Player puts it on the fridge beside the others.
End of Chapter 31

chapters.title: CHAPTER 32: THE RECORDING THAT STAYS OFF

steps.text: Scene: Mr. P's kitchen. Sunday afternoon. The Player has brought leftovers from the station potluck. The second chair is pulled out. The speaker on the counter is silent. Mrs. P's recording has not played in three weeks.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: I stopped starting it. Not because I don't want to hear her. Because I already know what she says. "Don't stay so late." I hear it when I want to. I don't need the speaker to say it for me anymore.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Does the chair still feel empty?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: Some days. Today it has your coat on it. That's different. The coat is not hers. It doesn't have to be.
They eat. The speaker stays off. When the Player leaves, Mr. P does not turn it on. He washes the dishes. The second chair stays where it is.

The recording is not destroyed. It is simply not playing. Mr. P can start it whenever he chooses. Tonight he chooses the sound of water in the sink and the memory of a voice he no longer needs a machine to carry. Both are real. Only one is in the room.
End of Chapter 32

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: Book Three continues. The ordinary days keep arriving. The echoes share space with popcorn, drawings, and coats on chairs. The writing remains open.

Scene: Lucella Mall, afternoon. The fountain in the center court runs again. Coins glitter at the bottom. The man from the carnival sits on the edge, not looking at the water. He has Georgie's Ferris wheel drawing in his lap. Penny and Georgie are nearby, looking at a store window. The Player stands a short distance away, watching the ordinary movement of people.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: I used to come here and wait for the sound to get louder. Now I come because the benches are comfortable and no one asks why I'm sitting alone. The drawing helps. When the sound tries to start, I look at the waving figure instead of the water.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (sitting beside him) Does it still try?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Man
steps.text: Less. When it does, I can tell it the kid is not at the top of anything. He's at school. Or at the park. Or drawing. The sound doesn't argue. It just gets quieter when I say it out loud.

The fountain does not remember the night a man stood in it fully clothed, listening for a child who was never there. The water only runs. The man chooses what he listens to instead. The drawing is creased from being folded and unfolded. It is still whole.

options.label: Ask if he wants to walk with Georgie and Penny for a while
Leave him with the fountain and the drawing
Tell him the station has a bench if the mall gets too loud
Buy a new notebook so he can write the sentences down when they arrive

steps.text: Main path: You sit until he folds the drawing again. He puts it in his pocket. He says he might go to the park later to see the new treehouse. You do not offer to go with him. He does not ask. Both of you stand when Georgie waves from the window.
End of Chapter 33

Scene: The old military outpost on the edge of the city. It has been turned into a community center. The fences are still there but the gates are open. Penny volunteers on Saturdays, helping sort donated clothes. Georgie is at a friend's house. The Player stops by with coffee.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (folding a small jacket) Some of these still have names written in the collars. I used to think if I found the right name I could give something back. Now I just make sure the jackets are clean. The names can stay. Or not. The kids who wear them will write new ones.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Do you ever hear the old sorry when you're here?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: Sometimes. When I pick up something small. It says "I should have held his hand." I answer it. I say "I am holding it now." Then I keep folding. It doesn't fill the room. The room is full of jackets.

The outpost is no longer a place where people waited for the infection to reach them. It is a place where jackets are sorted and coffee is drunk and a sentence is answered without becoming the only sound. Penny does not wear the bracelet today. It is in her pocket. She can put it on if she wants. She has not wanted to yet.

options.label: Help her sort the rest of the bin
Ask if she wants the bracelet out of her pocket
Tell her Georgie drew the outpost last week with the gates open
Sit on the loading dock and watch the city from the hill

steps.text: Main path: You help sort. She finds a jacket with no name. She writes "open" in the collar with a marker someone left behind. She does not explain. You do not ask. The coffee gets cold. Neither of you minds.
End of Chapter 34

chapters.title: CHAPTER 35: THE QUIET THAT IS CHOSEN

steps.text: Scene: The apartment. Late evening. All three chairs are occupied. Georgie is drawing at the table. Penny is reading. The Player is finishing a report on a laptop. The rain has started again, soft against the window. No one has spoken for twenty minutes. The silence is not empty.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (without looking up) I finished the new treehouse drawing. Do you want to see it?

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: After this chapter.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: After this paragraph.

Georgie waits. He does not repeat the question. When Penny closes her book and the Player saves the file, he turns the paper around. The new treehouse is in the center. Three figures stand on the platform. One is smaller. One has a bracelet. One wears a coat that looks like the Player's. In the background, the station. The badge. The mall fountain. The carnival wheel. All small. All present. No red. No empty chairs.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I didn't leave anyone out this time.

The drawing is not a promise that nothing will ever get loud again. It is a record of a night when three people sat in three chairs and no one had to fill the silence with a sentence they had already said. The rain continues. The drawing stays on the table until someone decides where it will hang. The story does not end. It simply reaches a place where it can rest.

options.label: Hang the drawing above the table
Ask Georgie if he wants to take it to the new treehouse
Leave it on the table for the night
Tell them both that the station log from last week had no red calls

steps.text: Main path: The drawing stays on the table. In the morning it will move to the wall. Tonight it is enough that it exists and that all three of them have seen it. The rain keeps tapping. No one turns on the old music box. No one needs to.
End of Chapter 35

chapters.title: CHAPTER 36: A NOTE UNDER THE BADGE

steps.text: Scene: The station. Morning. The Player arrives to find a new note pinned beneath Doggy's badge. The handwriting is careful. It is not Doggy's. It is not the Player's.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Note
steps.text: "The pie was never in the oven. Thank you for sitting with it anyway. —The woman from the 2 a.m. call."

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (reading it twice) She came in.
The note does not replace the one that says "Don't hesitate to live." It sits beside it. Both are true. The station keeps them both. The Player does not take either one down.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: Book Three reaches a resting place. The echoes have not vanished. They have learned to share the walls with new notes, new drawings, and chairs that are sometimes empty and sometimes not. The city of Lucella continues. The writing can continue. For now, the table has three chairs and the badge has two notes. That is enough for this chapter of the living.
THE END OF BOOK THREE

chapters.title: CHAPTER 37: THE TABLE WITH THREE CHAIRS

steps.text: Background: The apartment. Morning light through the window. The rain has stopped. The drawing Georgie finished the night before still sits on the table, creased but whole. Three chairs. Penny pours coffee. Georgie is already at the table with a new sheet of paper. The Player stands at the window, watching the street.
The night passed without the music box. No one turned it on. The silence stayed. In the morning the drawing is still there. It has not moved itself. Someone will have to decide where it hangs.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: (holding up the new paper) I started another one. This one is just the table. With the chairs. And us. But smaller. So it can fit in my pocket if I want to take it somewhere.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (setting a mug in front of him) You can hang the big one first. Then the pocket one can travel.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (turning from the window) The note at the station is still there. Both of them. Doggy's and the woman's. I didn't take either down.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Can I see the station one day? The real one. Not just in the drawing.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: When the log stays quiet for a full week. Then yes.
The condition is not a refusal. It is a measure. The echoes still speak sometimes. They do not fill the room anymore. The room has three chairs and a drawing that includes everyone who is still here.

options.label: Hang Georgie's drawing above the table now
Take Georgie to the station today anyway
Ask Penny if she wants the bracelet on the table too
Write a note of your own and pin it beside the others at the station

steps.text: Main path: You hang the drawing. Georgie watches to make sure it is straight. Penny steps back. The three of you look at it. No one says the word "sorry." The coffee cools. The street outside is ordinary. That is the ending that is still being written.
End of Chapter 37

chapters.title: CHAPTER 38: THE WEEK THAT STAYED QUIET

steps.text: Background: The station. One week later. The log on the desk has no red entries. The two notes under the badge are still there. The Player sits across from Doggy's empty desk. The chair is not empty. A woman from the 2 a.m. call sits in it, holding a thermos.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Woman
steps.text: I came back. Not for the pie. For the bench outside. It faces the street. I can sit there without anyone asking me if I am still waiting.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The log is quiet. Georgie can visit now. If you want company on the bench, the door is open.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Woman
steps.text: I might. Not every day. Some mornings the voice is louder. Some mornings it is just weather.

The station does not close. It does not need to. The echoes still arrive. They arrive with names now. The woman does not ask the Player to take the note down. The Player does not offer. Both notes stay. The thermos steams. Outside, the street is ordinary.

options.label: Invite Georgie and Penny to the station this afternoon
Sit with the woman on the bench for a while
Add a third note: "The door stays open."
Call Mr. P and tell him the plant is still empty

steps.text: Main path: You call Georgie. He brings the pocket drawing. Penny comes with coffee for three. The woman stays on the bench. No one fills the silence with an old sentence. The week stays quiet enough.
End of Chapter 38
Background: The old laboratory annex. Dust on the shelves. The apparatus is cold. Mr. P stands with his hands in his pockets. The Player waits by the door. No red liquid remains.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: I keep the recording off. Not because I have stopped missing her. Because the sentence is already mine. I can say it without the speaker.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The city is still here. The chairs are still here. The plant is empty. That is the part that stays true.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: (looking at an empty vial) I poured the rest out. I do not regret the pouring. I regret the nights I did not come home. Those nights are not in the vial. They are in the room I still walk through.

The laboratory does not need to be destroyed. It needs to stay empty. Mr. P locks the door when he leaves. He does not throw the key away. He puts it on the same ring as the house key. Both rooms remain. Neither one is the only one.

options.label: Walk with him back to the apartment
Ask if he wants to meet Georgie
Leave the key where it is
Tell him the woman from the station is still sitting on the bench

steps.text: Main path: You walk. He does not turn the recording on. The apartment has four chairs now. The fourth one is for whoever needs it. The drawing hangs above the table. The echoes share the wall. They do not own it.
End of Chapter 39

chapters.title: CHAPTER 40: THE DOOR THAT STAYS OPEN

steps.text: Background: The apartment. Evening. Four chairs. Georgie, Penny, the Player, and Mr. P. The drawing hangs on the wall. The pocket version sits on the table. Outside, the streetlights are on. No music box. No red. No empty seats that demand to be filled.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I drew the station with the door open. And the bench. And the woman. She can be in the picture if she wants. Or not. The door is open either way.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: The bracelet is in my pocket. I can put it on. Or I can leave it. Both are true.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: The recording stays off. The sentence is still mine.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The notes stay under the badge. The log can stay quiet. Or it can get loud again. We will sit with it either way.

The story reaches the place it was always moving toward. Not the absence of regret. The presence of the people who remain. The chairs are occupied. The door is open. The echoes can speak. They are no longer the only voice in the room. The city of Lucella continues. The table has room. The station keeps the notes. That is the ending that holds.

options.label: Leave the door open
Hang the pocket drawing beside the large one
Sit until the streetlights come on
Thank them for staying

steps.text: Main path: You sit. No one turns anything on. The rain does not come tonight. The drawing stays on the wall. The notes stay at the station. The story rests here. It is finished because the people in the room are still here. The echoes remain. They share the space. That is enough.
THE END

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: System Message
steps.text: The full story is complete. The regrets have not vanished. They have learned to live beside the chairs that are occupied and the door that stays open. Thank you for remaining with the echoes.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 41: THE WOMAN ON THE BENCH

steps.text: Background: The station platform. Late afternoon. The rain has returned lightly. The woman from the 2 a.m. call sits on the bench. The door of the station is open behind her. A paper bag rests beside her. No red light. No music box.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Woman
steps.text: You left the note under the badge. I read it. The pie was never in the oven. I still came.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (sitting beside her, not too close) The station stays open either way.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Woman
steps.text: My daughter used to wait here. She would draw on the back of the tickets. I still have one. It has a treehouse on it. And three figures. One of them is waving.
The echoes do not leave. They learn the shape of the bench. The woman does not ask the Player to make the drawing real. She only asks if the station still keeps the notes.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: Both notes are still there. The one about the pie. The one about living. They sit next to each other.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Woman
steps.text: Good. Then I can sit here without having to fill the empty seat with a sentence I already said.

options.label: Ask if she wants to meet Georgie
Sit in silence until the next train
Offer her the pocket drawing
Tell her the door will stay open

steps.text: Main path: You sit. The train arrives. No one gets off who needs to be apologized to. The woman folds the ticket drawing and puts it in her pocket. The station log does not record the hour. Some hours do not need to be written down.
End of Chapter 41

Background: The apartment backyard. Evening. A new treehouse sits between the old oak and the fence. Georgie is inside with a flashlight. The drawing of the station hangs on the wall of the treehouse. Four chairs are drawn on the floor in chalk.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I put the woman on the bench in the picture. She can stay or go. The door is open in the drawing too.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: (from below) Leo is coming tomorrow. He wants to see if the bracelet still fits.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (climbing up) The station note is still there. She came in.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: Then the treehouse has room for her drawing too. I left space.

The infection did not take the ability to make space. It only made the space feel smaller until someone drew the chairs again. Georgie draws a fifth figure on the edge of the paper. The figure is holding a paper bag. It is not labeled.

options.label: Help hang the station drawing
Ask Georgie what the fifth figure is holding
Leave the flashlight on for the night
Tell Penny the bracelet can stay in the pocket

steps.text: Main path: The drawing hangs. The flashlight stays on. In the morning the chalk chairs are still on the floor. No one erases them. The city of Lucella has one more treehouse that keeps the door open.
End of Chapter 42

Background: The locked laboratory annex. Mr. P stands outside the door. The key ring is in his hand. The house key and the lab key hang together. He does not open the door. The recording device is in his other hand. It is off.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: I still hear her when I want to. The speaker is not required. The sentence is mine.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The woman from the station is sitting on the bench. She has a ticket drawing of a treehouse.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: Then the keys can stay on the ring. The door can stay locked. Both rooms remain. Neither one has to be the only one.
He puts the key ring in his pocket. The laboratory does not need to be destroyed. It needs to stay empty. The echoes share the wall with the apartment. They do not own it.

options.label: Walk back to the apartment with him
Ask if he wants to see the treehouse
Leave the key where it is
Tell him the recording can stay off

steps.text: Main path: You walk. He does not turn the recording on. The apartment has four chairs. The fifth is for whoever needs it. The drawing hangs above the table. The echoes share the wall. They do not own it.
End of Chapter 43
Background: The police station. Morning. The log book is open on the desk. Two notes are under Doggy's badge. The Player writes one line and then stops.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: (writing) Station remains open. No red calls. The woman from the 2 a.m. call sat on the bench. She left with the ticket drawing.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Doggy
steps.text: (from the doorway) You don't have to fill every line. Some hours are just hours.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The pie note is still there. So is the one about living. They sit next to each other.

The log does not need to get loud again. It can stay quiet. The station keeps both notes. The city of Lucella continues. The table has room. The treehouse has chalk chairs. The laboratory stays locked. The door of the station stays open.

options.label: Close the log
Pin a new note about the treehouse
Leave the desk as it is
Tell Doggy the bracelet is still in Penny's pocket

steps.text: Main path: You close the log. The notes stay under the badge. In the evening the streetlights come on. No one turns anything on that does not need to be on. The story rests because the people are still here.
End of Chapter 44

chapters.title: CHAPTER 45: THE DOOR THAT STAYS OPEN FOREVER

steps.text: Background: The apartment. Night. Four chairs around the table. Georgie, Penny, the Player, and Mr. P. The drawing hangs on the wall. The pocket drawing sits beside the large one. Outside, the streetlights are on. The rain has stopped. No music box. No red. No empty seats that demand to be filled.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Georgie
steps.text: I drew the woman on the bench. And the treehouse. And the locked door. The door in the picture is open anyway.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Penny
steps.text: The bracelet is in my pocket. Leo can try it tomorrow. Or not. Both are true.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Mr. P
steps.text: The recording stays off. The key ring stays in my pocket. The sentence is still mine.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Player
steps.text: The notes stay under the badge. The log is closed. The station stays open. We will sit with it either way.

The story reaches the place it was always moving toward. Not the absence of regret. The presence of the people who remain. The chairs are occupied. The door is open. The echoes can speak. They are no longer the only voice in the room. The city of Lucella continues. The table has room. The station keeps the notes. The treehouse keeps the chalk. The laboratory stays empty. That is the ending that holds.

options.label: Leave the door open
Hang both drawings together
Sit until the streetlights go out
Thank them for staying

steps.text: Main path: You sit. No one turns anything on. The rain does not come tonight. The drawings stay on the wall. The notes stay at the station. The story rests here. It is finished because the people in the room are still here. The echoes remain. They share the space. That is enough.
THE END
